audit.whatIsWrong: Three chart rows are wrong on both layers. Packet is Garen, Garen, Garen, Garen, Garen, Yone, Yone; the pages read Garen, Skill, Yone, Yone, Garen, Yone, Yone — so levels 2, 3 and 4-5 are handed to Yone or called even.
audit.why: whys[1] 'Yone stays fragile at 2 while your silence-auto combo out-damages him', whys[2] 'Your Q-E all-in with silence beats squishy Yone before items at 3', whys[3] 'Through 4-5 you win any trade when his E Soul Unbound is down'. The early prose says 'You win levels 1-2 comfortably' and mid says 'Levels 3-6 stay yours'. A 54.44% win rate over 5231 games backs it. Only the tokens dissent.
audit.corrected: Level 2, Level 3 and Levels 4-5 -> Garen 6/10. Level 1 and Level 6 already read Garen; First item and 2+ items already read Yone.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] says to execute Yone 'so his second dash-back can't save the low-HP body'. Fate Sealed has no dash-back.
audit.why: Riot's R text: 'Yone blinks behind the last champion in a line with a slash so powerful it pulls all enemies hit towards him.' It is one blink plus a pull — there is no return dash. The dash-back belongs to Soul Unbound (E), a separate 22s ability. Inventing a second dash tells the player to hold R for an escape that does not exist. What actually matters is that the R leaves him standing in melee range with you pulled to him — inside your 400-range execute.
audit.corrected: Describe Fate Sealed as a blink-behind plus pull that plants him next to you, and execute on the threshold rather than waiting for a phantom second dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Cleave (W) appears nowhere on the page, and report[5] does not say where the punish window physically is during Soul Unbound.
audit.why: Spirit Cleave is a 14s cone that shields Yone, scaling with the number of champions hit, and its cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed — in a 1v1 it is a small shield on a short timer, so grinding past it beats trying to burst through it. Soul Unbound: 'Yone's spirit leaves his body behind' and at the end 'Yone's spirit is forced back to his body'. The body is a fixed point you can stand on and hit; the cooldown is 22s at rank 1 falling to 10s at rank 5.
audit.corrected: Name Spirit Cleave with its 14s shield, and make the Soul Unbound advice concrete: hit the body, he returns to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization buys Executioner's Calling first back and prioritises Mortal Reminder third, both justified as 'his healing breaks your trade math'. Yone has no healing.
audit.why: Nothing in Yone's kit heals — the passive is bonus magic damage on every second attack plus crit chance, Q is damage and a knockup, W is a shield, E repeats a portion of damage dealt, R is a blink and pull. No heal flag appears on any slot. Buying Grievous Wounds against him is dead gold. His damage is genuinely mixed (passive magic every second attack, plus Spirit Cleave), which is what the boots and third item should answer.
audit.corrected: Drop the anti-heal rush, take Mercury's Treads for his magic component, and put a mixed-damage item third.
sources: enemyKit P/Q/W/E/R flags — no heal anywhere

edits.before: Track Yone’s Soul Unbound (22s): He snaps back when it ends. Punish that spot. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1, 10s maxed. His body stays put — hit the body, not the spirit, and he snaps back to it.

edits.before: Get hit by his Q3. Fight during his E burst. Extend into his R. Treat your ultimate as a verdict, never as harassment.
edits.after: Get hit by his Q3. Fight during his E burst. Ignore Spirit Cleave — it is a 14s cone that shields him, so grind past it.

edits.before: Start Doran's Blade + Health Potion. First back: Executioner's Calling (≈800g) — his healing breaks your trade math. Core: Stridebreaker  (run-downs stop flipping at the last second) → Phantom Dancer  (spin DPS + the MS to stick); boots: Plated Steelcaps. Spike: Mortal Reminder third — priority, his healing fights your execute; your Q-MS run-down + R execute closes any HP lead you bank.
edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + Health Potion. First back: Tiamat / Phage + boots (≈1300g) — Yone has no heal in his kit, so skip Executioner's. Core: Stridebreaker  (run-downs stop flipping at the last second) → Phantom Dancer  (spin DPS + the MS to stick); boots: Mercury's Treads — his passive hits magic every second attack. Spike: Force of Nature third against his mixed damage; your Q-MS run-down + R execute closes any HP lead.

edits.before: Demacian Justice punishes Yone's ult commitment: when he Fate Sealed dashes in, execute him after his Q3 lands so his second dash-back can't save the low-HP body.
edits.after: Demacian Justice punishes his commit: Fate Sealed blinks him behind you and pulls you in, so he ends up inside your 400-range execute — spend R the moment he is under it.

notes: Level-chart edits are one atomic group (content win[1..3] plus full phases[1]/[2]/[3] side+rating); after the flip both layers match the packet chart row for row. Two substantive corrections beyond the chart: (1) Fate Sealed has no second dash-back — that was invented, and the page told players to time their 120s ultimate around it; (2) the itemization rushed Grievous Wounds against a champion with zero healing in his kit, which is dead gold in a lane the data says Garen is already winning. I did not touch the 'Q3' shorthand: Riot's text says the empowered cast comes at 2 stacks of Gathering Storm, and whether the community 'Q3' label maps to that cleanly is a presentation call for the user, not a fact I can verify — see questionsForUser.
